timer.note: RDTSC (LFENCE+RDTSC to open, RDTSCP to close) replaces clock_gettime because the latter costs more than several of the operations being measured. Any figure at or below floor_ns is NOT a measurement of the code -- it is the timer.

cpu_placement.note: macOS exposes affinity TAGS, not pinning: the kernel is asked to co-locate tagged threads on one L2 and may ignore it. Tail latency here includes migrations that a Linux box with isolcpus would not have. Single NUMA node, so remote-memory cost does not arise on this host.

measurements.name: book.upsert
measurements.note: one level update, the operation a feed handler performs most

measurements.name: book.top_of_book
measurements.note: the most frequently called read in the system

measurements.name: book.depth_10
measurements.note: 10-level snapshot into caller storage, no allocation

measurements.name: feed.validate
measurements.note: sequence + timestamp + band + EWMA outlier check

measurements.name: risk.pretrade_check
measurements.note: kill switch -> limits -> collar -> position, full gate

measurements.name: fix.parse_validated
measurements.note: full validation: BodyLength + CheckSum, what a real engine pays

measurements.name: fix.parse_trusted
measurements.note: framing trusted -- only legitimate replaying a trusted log

measurements.name: tick_to_order
measurements.note: validate -> book -> top-of-book -> pre-trade -> encode. NO network, NO kernel, NO venue.

measurements.name: handoff.spsc_lockfree
measurements.note: one message across an EMPTY queue. Cache-line separated indices, acquire/release, cached opposite index.

measurements.name: handoff.spsc_false_shared
measurements.note: IDENTICAL logic, indices packed into ONE cache line -- the measured cost of false sharing.

measurements.name: handoff.mutex_condvar
measurements.note: std::queue + mutex + condition_variable, paced identically. The wake-up is a syscall and the tail is a scheduling quantum.

environment_note: In-process, single machine, general-purpose kernel. NO CPU pinning, NO isolated cores, NO tickless mode, NO hugepages, NO kernel-bypass networking. A real low-latency deployment controls all of those. Read it this way: the p50 describes the code, the tail describes this host.
tail_note: p99_over_p50 is the number to read first. A ratio near 1 is a predictable path; a large one means the median is not describing the system's behaviour.
